## Natural history notes

A tall native perennial bunchgrass characterized by broad, arching leaves and large, showy silvery-white to purplish flower plumes that rise well above the foliage in late summer and fall. Sugarcane Plumegrass occurs primarily in moist to wet open habitats, including pine flatwoods, wet prairies, marsh margins, ditches, and other seasonally saturated areas. In Florida, it is widespread and can form conspicuous clumps that provide vertical structure within wetland and flatwoods vegetation. Its current accepted name is often given as Saccharum giganteum, with Erianthus giganteus treated as a synonym.
